properties.name: Pair two designs by complementary role, so the seam is computed rather than hand-wired
properties.statement:
Anthony's idea (2026-07-27), and the analogy he reached for is load-bearing rather than decorative: RNA strands pair because the bases are COMPLEMENTARY — adenine with uracil, guanine with cytosine — never like-with-like. Applied here: each boundary declares a ROLE — it publishes, it subscribes, it does both, or it is not external at all — and each project publishes only its publish-or-both boundaries with an id and a description. Combining two designs then starts mechanically: match every publisher against every subscriber, associate them, and treat the pair as ONE graph for every ordinary reflow2 check — gaps, defects, god nodes, surprising connections. The pairing is what makes composition cheap; everything after it already exists (cap:composed-analysis).

DECIDED 2026-07-27 (dec:pairing-role-placement, accepted on Anthony's word): the role lives on the INTERFACE, extending `designation`, not on every node. A Component both publishes and subscribes, so a per-node role collapses to `both` and pairs with everything — the `both` value was the tell that the attribute was on the wrong noun.

WHAT REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS. `Interface.designation` is the publish flag (`internal | published`, defaulting to internal because publishing is a commitment). `export_surface` emits published Interfaces plus the Components either side and withholds the rest. `PROVIDES` and `CONSUMES` carry the two roles at the edge level. The publish half works end to end.

WHAT IS MISSING, and it is the whole idea: THE SUBSCRIBE SIDE IS NOT DECLARABLE. A design says what it OFFERS; it cannot say what it NEEDS from outside in a form another design can be matched against. Today a need is a CONSUMES edge pointing at an Interface the consumer modelled INSIDE ITS OWN design — so a match only happens where the consumer already guessed the provider's contract and named it compatibly. Without that half there is no complementary strand.

THREE OUTCOMES, ALL USEFUL: a publisher matched to a subscriber (the seam, computed); a publisher nobody subscribes to (dead surface); a subscriber nothing publishes (an unmet need — the loudest signal there is). Two publishers of one key is a fourth: a duplicated provider, a conflict rather than a match.

THE PAIRING KEY IS NOT NAME ALONE — AMENDED 2026-07-28 AFTER A REAL TRIAL. Complementary role plus a matching key was the first draft, and the dynograph-foundation session refuted it from the provider's side within an hour of the channel opening. Their design carries three `medium: REST` boundaries: `ifc:rest-v1` (TCP, JWT), `ifc:uds` (Unix socket, JWT, `transport_security: physical`) and `ifc:ops-probes` (PUBLIC AND UNAUTHENTICATED BY DESIGN, because an orchestrator's liveness check cannot hold a credential). Under role-plus-medium alone, a consumer declaring "I require REST" pairs against all three — including the unauthenticated probe surface. That is not a near-miss; it is the pairing rule confidently producing a wrong and security-relevant answer.

So base-compatibility is `medium` PLUS `transport_security` PLUS `auth`. Every one of those is already a property on Interface, put there by req:interface-spec-complete; the fault was leaving them out of the key, not a missing field. And the analogy survives the correction better than it started: adenine–uracil is two hydrogen bonds, guanine–cytosine three. COMPATIBILITY WAS NEVER A SINGLE POINT OF CONTACT.

A mismatch on those axes must be REPORTED AS AN INCOMPATIBILITY, never dropped as a non-match. "You publish this, I need this, and we cannot be connected the way either of us is built" is exactly the finding worth having, and silence would hide it.

NAMES ARE STILL FUZZY. `auth-api` against `AuthService` is the Bob/Bobby/Robert problem, already solved once: ingest's two-band resolution (below fuzzy_threshold = no match, between = a reported candidate, above auto_merge_threshold = act) plus the token-subset pass that catches `Gateway` vs `API Gateway`. Reuse that rather than inventing a second matcher, and ASK about the middle band (dec:ask-not-repair).

UNLABELLED MUST NOT READ AS `non_external`. A boundary nobody classified silently counting as internal means a design that never did the labelling pairs with nothing and reports a clean seam — the blindness cap:coverage exists to end. The pairing report must count and name what carries no role, as coverage_report does.
